notes: No ad-free copy exists for this Audioboom feed, so there are no INSERTED markers. Every ad below was found by reading the transcript; delivery is marked 'produced' from the ad-copy style itself (third-person, brand-scripted, not Adam's conversational voice), not confirmed by a byte comparison.
Fingerprinting found 0:00:00-0:01:10 matches the previous episode's audio (across): that is the eBay Live + Viori preroll, split into two regions here since they are two sponsors read back to back.

The Wegovi spot ('Every game day, you show up for your team... Ask your prescriber about Wegovi...') plays twice, verbatim, within this episode (fingerprint 'within' at 0:17:37-0:18:08 and 0:24:18-0:24:49). The recognizer transcribed it slightly differently each time ('weekovi' vs 'week OV'; a trailing comma vs a period), which is what the anchors below use to tell the two instances apart without ambiguity.

The 'Star Spangled Banner... give us our theme... March Madness' bit at 0:01:12-0:01:42 is a cold-open tease: it is the exact same audio as real conversation later at 0:26:47-0:27:17 (fingerprint 'within'), replayed at the top as a hook before the formal welcome. It is not a paid ad, so it is marked EITHER/INTRO rather than ADVERTISEMENT; the 0:26:47 occurrence is ordinary conversation and is left unlabelled.
0:01:42-0:02:11 has no transcript (crosstalk or an edit the recognizer skipped) and is not covered by any fingerprint hit, so it is left unlabelled rather than guessed.

0:59:22-0:59:55 (fingerprint 'across') falls in the untranscribed gap between the sign-off ('I was thinking I'm not...') and the NBC promo ('Monday on NBC...'). It is almost certainly the show's wordless outro sting reused episode to episode, so it is bridged with start_at_end_of/end_until and marked EITHER rather than guessed as speech.

1:00:04-1:00:34 (fingerprint 'across') is the NBC 'On Fire' TV promo, a national syndicated spot that would run unchanged across episodes; scored as ADVERTISEMENT like the ChatGPT read that follows it at the very end of the file.

Short NORMAL regions were added after each ad so an over-long cut would show up in scoring. All anchors keep the recognizer's exact wording, typos included. Regions are listed in strict time order, since the checker's anchors resolve by scanning forward from the previous region.
